daily_brief: The collapse of US-Canada trade negotiations dominates today's headlines, with Prime Minister Mark Carney announcing retaliatory tariffs 'dollar-for-dollar' after President Trump imposed 50% duties on approximately $20 billion in Canadian goods [BBC, Al Jazeera, Le Monde]. The breakdown marks an unprecedented rupture between the longtime allies, with Carney declaring the countries are now in a trade 'war.' In Ukraine, rescue operations continue at a Kryvyi Rih shopping centre where a Russian double-tap drone strike killed 16 people and injured over 130 [BBC, Le Monde, RFI]. France responded by pledging interceptor missiles to bolster Ukraine's depleted air defences. The DRC's Ebola outbreak has become the deadliest in the country's history, with 2,325 confirmed deaths and the UN warning the virus 'is winning' [The Guardian]. In Sweden, police confirmed a 17-year-old girl was killed in a sword attack at a high school in Fagersta, with an 18-year-old suspect in custody [BBC]. Meanwhile, Chinese humanoid robots captured global attention by breaking Usain Bolt's 100m world record at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing [The Hindu, Al Jazeera].

top_stories.headline: US-Canada Trade Talks Collapse, Triggering Escalating Tariff War Between Longtime Allies
bullets: Trump imposed 50% tariffs on approximately $20 billion in Canadian goods after negotiations broke down Friday, citing Canada wanting 'benefits of being a State, without being one'
Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Canada will match US tariffs 'dollar-for-dollar' from September 8, covering steel, dairy, appliances, and electronics
Both sides blamed last-minute changes for torpedoing the deal, with Carney stating the US 'asked too much and offered too little'
The collapse upends decades of free trade between the countries with no clear path to resolution

top_stories.headline: Russian Double-Tap Drone Strike Kills 16 at Ukrainian Shopping Centre, France Pledges Missiles
bullets: Two drones hit a busy shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih in quick succession Friday, killing 16 and injuring over 130 people; four remain missing
The second drone deliberately targeted emergency workers responding to the first strike, a tactic condemned by Zelensky as 'cynical and despicable'
France announced it will deliver interceptor missiles to Ukraine, with Macron saying Russia's targeting of civilians 'signals an admission of weakness'
Zelensky said Ukraine lacks sufficient air defence missiles, stating 'interceptors for the Patriots have not yet been replaced'

top_stories.headline: DRC Ebola Outbreak Becomes Country's Deadliest, UN Warns Virus 'Is Winning'
bullets: At least 2,325 people have died, surpassing the 2018-20 outbreak toll, with confirmed cases reaching 4,945
The WHO says the outbreak is on track to become the largest in history, surpassing west Africa's 2014-16 epidemic of 11,325 deaths
The rare Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccines or treatments; one person dies approximately every 30 minutes
Six of DRC's 26 provinces are affected, with over 3,400 cases in Ituri province where the outbreak began

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Comprehensive coverage emphasizing the outbreak's record-breaking pace and lack of available treatments

top_stories.headline: Teenage Girl Killed in Sword Attack at Swedish High School
bullets: A 17-year-old girl was killed and two boys aged 12 and 17 were seriously injured at Brinell School in Fagersta, central Sweden
An 18-year-old man, reportedly a former student, was arrested; police fired shots during the response
The attack occurred on the first day students returned after summer break; the suspect was reportedly wearing a helmet
Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and opposition leader Magdalena Andersson visited the school Saturday

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Straightforward factual reporting with official statements from police and political leaders

top_stories.headline: Chinese Humanoid Robot Breaks Usain Bolt's 100m World Record at Beijing Games
bullets: A robot named 'Tianzhuo' ran 100m in 9.39 seconds, beating Bolt's 9.58 second world record at the World Humanoid Robot Games
Over 2,000 humanoid robots are participating in the five-day event featuring 51 categories including running, table tennis, and soccer
The games highlight China's rapid robotics progress amid escalating US-China technology competition
The US recently banned imports of foreign-made humanoid robots and added Chinese robotics firm Unitree to a Pentagon restricted list

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Detailed technical coverage placing event in context of US-China tech rivalry

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Brief video coverage focused on the record-breaking achievement
